findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
findings.body: The matcher returns false when the extracted shortcut EQUALS the expected one, so it rejects correct IDs and accepts wrong ones. The substring(3,5) is also wrong for the 6-char prefix `sstt gg`, where the grant shortcut is at indexes 4..6. The comment about the '4th char' reflects the old format. The assertion therefore never validates the grant type, and the tests that use it will fail or pass for the wrong reasons.

findings.title: Null check on wrong variable
findings.body: The `rawTokenId` null check is done on `grantType` (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId...")`), so a null rawTokenId is never rejected. This is a copy-paste bug.

findings.title: Token ID encoding throws for contexts without a registered grant type
findings.body: initToken encodes the ID using the GRANT_TYPE attribute on clientSessionCtx. Any code path creating access tokens that does not set this attribute falls back to "na". That is handled. However, grant types set from `context.getGrantType()` come from the raw form param, which may be null or differ from the factory id (e.g. when the Context is constructed by internal callers). A null grantType makes `clientSessionContext.getAttribute` return null and falls back to "na"; a non-registered string makes encodeTokenId throw IllegalStateException, which turns a token request into a 500.

findings.title: Lightweight detection uses session attribute and context client, not the token being created
findings.body: getShouldUseLightweightToken reads session.getContext().getClient(), which may not be the client the token is issued for (e.g. in token exchange or when the context client is null). That can mislabel the token type or cause an NPE.

findings.title: Shortcut uniqueness validation is ineffective
findings.body: Duplicate shortcuts or ids are detected only by comparing map sizes after puts to ConcurrentHashMaps. A duplicate shortcut overwrites the earlier entry, and the sizes may then still differ or match by coincidence. A grant type's shortcut that collides with "na" is also undetected. The lazy refresh paths also skip duplicate checks.
